data.title: bn-2t2e: install just-sealed packs via the lazy attach path
data.description:
seal_consolidated installed the eager verification parse-back, so a segment sealed in-process kept its whole pack (plus a second copy of its payload columns and the decoded event-type ids) resident for the life of the segment — the residency bn-dbz removed from reopen. After the durable write completes, the pack is now re-opened with open_pack (the reopen path) and THAT lazy index is installed.

Invariants deliberately untouched: (1) identity still comes from the verified parse-back of the exact bytes, not from the buffer and not from the re-open — the re-open must AGREE with it or it is not used; (2) ordering is unchanged — encode, verify, durable write (temp/fsync/rename/dir-fsync), footer names the pack, install-then-evict; the re-open sits between the durable write and the footer and only reads. A re-open that fails or disagrees falls back to the in-memory image (pre-bn-2t2e behaviour); a real disagreement is caught and converged by the reopen path's own identity check (bn-11g reader rule 3 / bn-30u).

Adds SealedSegmentIndex::resident_bytes() and one guard test (seal_consolidated_installs_the_pack_lazily) asserting a just-sealed segment retains exactly what a reopen retains, pinned against open_pack_eager as the pack-sized reference. Verified to fail against the old install.

Evidence: cargo nextest -p mess-index -p mess-store 444/444 pass; cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean; just fmt-check clean. Residency demo (16 payload-heavy segments, 32.35 MiB of packs): sum(resident_bytes) 33.9 MB -> 1008 B, process RSS delta +76.4 MiB -> +5.9 MiB.
